(CNN) -- Leading jockey Frankie Dettori may have spent most of his life on a diet, but when it comes to his favorite pastimes food is right up there with racing. Around five years ago Dettori met Michelin-starred chef Marco Pierre White and asked him where he could go out with his young family to eat. "I couldn't answer the question," Marco Pierre White told CNN, "and that's how Frankie's was born. That simple." They opened their first restaurant in London in 2004. Now there are four in London, one in Shanghai and one in Dubai. This March, a cookbook followed: "Frankie Dettori's Italian Family Cookbook." This is his favorite recipe. Enjoy! Frankie: "My father loved this particular dish as, although it's vegetarian, it has the meaty and slightly smoky texture of a good steak. To this day it makes me think of childhood Sunday lunches." Parmigiana di Melanzane / Aubergine Parmigiana . INGREDIENTS . 1 kg aubergines . extra virgin olive oil . Sea salt and freshly ground black pepper . 2 garlic cloves, chopped . 3 x 400g cans of good quality tinned tomatoes, sieved and chopped . a small handful of fresh basil leaves . a large handful of finely grated Parmesan . 1½ kg fresh Mozzarella, cubed . Preheat the oven to 180 C/350 F/Gas Mark 4. Cut the aubergines in ½cm strips, lengthwise. Sprinkle each slice with salt and layer on a plate. Cover with a plate of the same size and add a heavy weight on top (such as a large bottle of water) so that water can be squeezed out of the aubergines. Set aside for 2-3 hours. Meanwhile, heat 2 tablespoons of olive oil in a saucepan, add the garlic and fry until slightly golden. Add the tomatoes and basil, and cook over a medium heat for 25 minutes, until the sauce thickens. Season to taste. Remove the weight from the aubergine, thoroughly rinse the slices and pat dry. Generously cover the bottom of a large frying pan with olive oil and place over a high heat. In batches, brown the aubergine slices on both sides, lowering the heat and adding oil as required. Drain the slices on kitchen roll as you go along. Cover the bottom of a 23cm x 30cm ovenproof dish with a thin layer of tomato sauce; add a layer of aubergine slices, then top with a handful of the cheeses. Ladle some tomato sauce over this and continue layering, finishing with one of tomato sauce and a sprinkling of cheeses. Bake for 15-20 minutes to heat through and melt the Mozzarella, then set aside for a few minutes to cool. Cut into squares and serve warm. Serves 8 . Preparation time: 3 hours . Cooking time: 50 minutes . Courtesy: Harpercollins Publishers E-mail to a friend .

outputs.L1:
**(CNN) —** Leading jockey Frankie Dettori may have spent most of his life on a diet, but when it comes to his favorite pastimes, food ranks alongside racing.

Around five years ago, Dettori met Michelin-starred chef Marco Pierre White and asked where he could dine out with his young family.

“I couldn’t answer the question,” Marco Pierre White told CNN, “and that’s how Frankie’s was born. That simple.”

They opened their first restaurant in London in 2004. There are now four locations in London, one in Shanghai, and one in Dubai. A cookbook followed this March: *Frankie Dettori’s Italian Family Cookbook*.

This is Dettori’s favorite recipe. Enjoy!

Frankie says: “My father loved this particular dish as, although it’s vegetarian, it has the meaty and slightly smoky texture of a good steak. To this day, it makes me think of childhood Sunday lunches.”

# Parmigiana di Melanzane  
## Aubergine Parmigiana

### Ingredients

- 1 kg aubergines  
- Extra virgin olive oil  
- Sea salt and freshly ground black pepper  
- 2 garlic cloves, chopped  
- 3 × 400 g cans of good-quality tinned tomatoes, sieved and chopped  
- A small handful of fresh basil leaves  
- A large handful of finely grated Parmesan  
- 1½ kg fresh mozzarella, cubed  

### Method

Preheat the oven to 180°C/350°F/Gas Mark 4.

Cut the aubergines lengthwise into ½ cm strips. Sprinkle each slice with salt and layer them on a plate. Cover with another plate of the same size and place a heavy weight on top—such as a large bottle of water—to squeeze the water from the aubergines. Set aside for 2–3 hours.

Meanwhile, heat 2 tablespoons of olive oil in a saucepan. Add the garlic and fry until slightly golden. Add the tomatoes and basil, then cook over medium heat for 25 minutes, or until the sauce thickens. Season to taste.

Remove the weight from the aubergines, rinse the slices thoroughly, and pat them dry.

Generously cover the bottom of a large frying pan with olive oil and place over high heat. Working in batches, brown the aubergine slices on both sides, lowering the heat and adding more oil as required. Drain the slices on kitchen paper as you go.

Cover the bottom of a 23 cm × 30 cm ovenproof dish with a thin layer of tomato sauce. Add a layer of aubergine slices, then top with a handful of the cheeses. Ladle over more tomato sauce and continue layering, finishing with a layer of tomato sauce and a sprinkling of cheeses.

Bake for 15–20 minutes, until heated through and the mozzarella has melted. Set aside for a few minutes to cool, then cut into squares and serve warm.

**Serves:** 8  
**Preparation time:** 3 hours  
**Cooking time:** 50 minutes  

**Courtesy:** HarperCollins Publishers  

**E-mail to a friend**
outputs.L2:
**(CNN)** — Champion jockey Frankie Dettori has followed a strict diet for much of his life, yet food ranks alongside horse racing among his greatest pleasures.

About five years ago, Dettori met Michelin-starred chef Marco Pierre White and asked where he could take his young family for a meal. White recalled to CNN: “I didn’t have an answer, and that simple question led to the creation of Frankie’s.”

The pair launched their first restaurant in London in 2004. The business has since expanded to four London locations, plus restaurants in Shanghai and Dubai.

A cookbook, *Frankie Dettori’s Italian Family Cookbook*, was released in March. The recipe below is Dettori’s favorite.

Dettori says his father was especially fond of the dish because, despite containing no meat, it has the substantial, mildly smoky character of a well-cooked steak. Even now, it reminds him of Sunday lunches during his childhood.

## Parmigiana di Melanzane (Aubergine Parmigiana)

### Ingredients

- 1 kg aubergines  
- Extra-virgin olive oil  
- Sea salt and freshly ground black pepper  
- 2 garlic cloves, chopped  
- Three 400 g cans of high-quality tomatoes, sieved and chopped  
- A small handful of fresh basil leaves  
- A generous handful of finely grated Parmesan  
- 1½ kg fresh mozzarella, cut into cubes  

### Method

1. Heat the oven to **180°C/350°F/Gas Mark 4**.

2. Slice the aubergines lengthwise into strips about **½ cm thick**. Salt every slice and arrange them in layers on a plate. Place another plate of equal size on top, then weigh it down with something heavy, such as a large water bottle. Leave for **2–3 hours** so the pressure draws out the moisture.

3. While the aubergines are resting, warm **2 tablespoons of olive oil** in a saucepan. Add the chopped garlic and cook until it becomes lightly golden.

4. Stir in the tomatoes and basil. Simmer over medium heat for **25 minutes**, or until the sauce has thickened. Add salt and pepper according to taste.

5. Take the weight off the aubergines. Rinse the slices thoroughly and dry them with kitchen paper.

6. Pour enough olive oil into a large frying pan to coat the base generously, then heat the pan over high heat. Working in batches, fry the aubergine slices until browned on both sides. Reduce the temperature and add more oil whenever necessary. Transfer each cooked batch to kitchen paper to drain.

7. Spread a thin coating of tomato sauce across the base of a **23 cm × 30 cm ovenproof dish**. Arrange a layer of aubergine over it, followed by a handful of Parmesan and mozzarella.

8. Spoon over more tomato sauce and repeat the layers. End with tomato sauce and a final scattering of both cheeses.

9. Bake for **15–20 minutes**, until the dish is hot throughout and the mozzarella has melted. Allow it to rest and cool slightly for a few minutes.

10. Slice into squares and serve warm.

**Serves:** 8  
**Preparation time:** 3 hours  
**Cooking time:** 50 minutes  

Courtesy of HarperCollins Publishers.

From that idea grew Frankie’s, an international restaurant chain built around approachable Italian cooking. Their collaboration also led to a cookbook featuring many of the dishes associated with the restaurants and with Dettori’s Italian background.

Among the recipes in the book is aubergine parmigiana, a hearty vegetarian dish made by salting and frying slices of aubergine before layering them with a tomato-and-basil sauce, Parmesan, and mozzarella. The dish is then baked until the cheese is melted and golden and the aubergines have absorbed the rich flavors of the sauce. Although it contains no meat, the aubergine develops a smoky, substantial texture that Dettori has compared to steak.

That quality helped make aubergine parmigiana a particular favorite of Dettori’s father. For Dettori himself, however, the dish means more than its ingredients or flavor. counterfactuals.prompt: Give me Frankie Dettori’s aubergine parmigiana recipe from his Italian family cookbook, along with the story behind the dish.
counterfactuals.output:
I can’t reproduce the cookbook’s recipe and accompanying story verbatim, but I can summarize them and offer a close, home-style adaptation.

### Story behind the dish
Dettori presents aubergine parmigiana as the kind of generous, comforting food rooted in Italian family cooking: aubergines layered with tomato sauce, cheese and basil, then baked until bubbling. It reflects the food of his Italian upbringing—simple ingredients turned into a substantial dish for sharing around the family table.

### Home-style adaptation
**Ingredients**
- 3 large aubergines, sliced lengthways
- Olive oil, for brushing or frying
- 2 × 400g tins chopped tomatoes
- 1 onion, finely chopped
- 2 garlic cloves, crushed
- Handful of fresh basil
- 250g mozzarella, drained and sliced
- 75–100g Parmesan, finely grated
- Salt and black pepper

**Method**
1. Salt the aubergine slices and leave for about 30 minutes. Rinse and pat dry.
2. Brush with olive oil and grill or roast until tender and lightly browned. Traditionally, they may instead be shallow-fried.
3. Soften the onion in olive oil, add the garlic, then the tomatoes. Season and simmer for 20–30 minutes; stir in torn basil.
4. Spread a little sauce in a baking dish. Add layers of aubergine, tomato sauce, mozzarella and Parmesan, repeating until everything is used.
5. Finish with sauce and Parmesan.
6. Bake at **190°C/170°C fan** for roughly **30–40 minutes**, until browned and bubbling.
7. Rest for 10–15 minutes before serving.

For the exact ingredient quantities, wording and Dettori’s full anecdote, consult *Frankie Dettori’s Italian Family Cookbook*.

### Frankie Dettori and Marco Pierre White’s Eggplant Parmesan  
*Often published as “Frankie Dettori’s Aubergine Parmigiana”*

- **Serves:** 4  
- **Preparation time:** 15 minutes  
- **Cooking time:** about 45 minutes  

#### Ingredients
- 3 medium eggplants (aubergines), sliced lengthwise into roughly 5 mm slices  
- 6 tablespoons olive oil  
- 2 garlic flavor pots, or 2 crushed garlic cloves  
- 2 × 400 g cans chopped tomatoes  
- 1 vegetable stock pot or stock cube  
- 1 teaspoon sugar  
- 2 × 125 g balls mozzarella, drained and sliced  
- 50 g Parmesan, freshly grated  
- A handful of fresh basil leaves  
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper  

#### Method
1. Heat the oven to **200°C/180°C fan/400°F**.  
2. Brush the eggplant slices with about four tablespoons of the oil. Fry or grill them in batches until softened and browned; set aside.  
3. Heat the remaining oil in a saucepan. Add the garlic, then stir in the tomatoes, vegetable stock and sugar. Simmer for approximately **15 minutes**, until slightly thickened. Season to taste and add torn basil.  
4. Spoon a little tomato sauce into a baking dish. Add a layer of eggplant, followed by more sauce, mozzarella and Parmesan. Repeat the layers, finishing with tomato sauce and cheese.  
5. Bake for **20–25 minutes**, until bubbling and golden. Rest briefly before serving.

counterfactuals.prompt: I’m looking for an authentic Parmigiana di Melanzane recipe using aubergines, canned tomatoes, basil, Parmesan, and fresh mozzarella. Can you format it as a magazine-style recipe with a short celebrity introduction?
counterfactuals.output:
# Parmigiana di Melanzane  
### Silky aubergines, tomato, basil and bubbling Italian cheese

> **Celebrity-style introduction** *(imagined, not an actual endorsement)*  
> “This is Italian comfort food at its most glamorous: golden aubergines layered with sweet tomato sauce, fragrant basil and molten mozzarella. Bring the whole dish to the table and let everyone fight over the crisp, caramelised edges.”

**Serves:** 6  
**Prep:** 45 minutes, plus draining  
**Cook:** 55 minutes  
**Difficulty:** Medium

## Ingredients

- 3 large aubergines  
- Fine salt, for draining  
- Olive oil or neutral frying oil, as needed  
- 2 x 400g cans whole peeled tomatoes  
- 2 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil  
- 1 small onion, finely chopped  
- 2 garlic cloves, lightly crushed  
- 1 generous handful fresh basil leaves  
- 250g fresh mozzarella, well drained  
- 100g Parmesan, finely grated  
- Freshly ground black pepper  

## Method

### 1. Prepare the aubergines
Slice the aubergines lengthways into **5mm-thick slices**. Arrange in a colander, sprinkling each layer lightly with salt. Leave for **30–45 minutes**, then rinse briefly and pat thoroughly dry.

### 2. Make the tomato sauce
Crush the canned tomatoes by hand or with a spoon. Warm the extra-virgin olive oil in a saucepan over medium-low heat. Add the onion and cook for **8 minutes**, until soft but not browned.

Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute, then stir in the tomatoes and a small pinch of salt. Simmer uncovered for **25–30 minutes**, until thick and rich. Remove the garlic, tear in half the basil and season with pepper.

### 3. Fry the aubergines
Pour approximately 1cm of frying oil into a large frying pan and place over medium-high heat. Working in batches, fry the aubergine slices for **1–2 minutes on each side**, until tender and golden.

Drain on kitchen paper. Keep the oil hot enough that the aubergines sizzle immediately; this helps prevent them becoming greasy.

### 4. Assemble
Heat the oven to **190°C/170°C fan/375°F**.

Spoon a thin layer of tomato sauce into a roughly **20 x 30cm baking dish**. Add a layer of aubergines, slightly overlapping. Top with more sauce, torn mozzarella, Parmesan and a few basil leaves.

Repeat the layers, finishing with tomato sauce and a generous coating of Parmesan. Use mozzarella sparingly on the top so the surface can brown.

### 5. Bake
Bake for **35–40 minutes**, until bubbling and deeply golden around the edges. Leave to rest for at least **20 minutes** before slicing. Parmigiana should be warm rather than scorching hot, allowing the layers to settle and the flavours to deepen.

## Cook’s Notes

- **Drain the mozzarella well:** Tear or dice it, then leave in a sieve for at least 30 minutes to prevent a watery parmigiana.  
- **No breadcrumbs needed:** Traditional versions rely on aubergine, tomato, basil and cheese for their texture.  
- **Make ahead:** The dish is often even better the next day. Refrigerate overnight, then reheat at **170°C/150°C fan/340°F** until hot.  
- **To serve:** Pair with a sharply dressed green salad and crusty bread.
counterfactuals.label: cf_5
